column1: Hettie|I would have offered it an apple.|And spoiled it for every sensible meal after that. You and that cow would have got along terribly well.
Gwil|I could help plant a few.|Bring a spade when you have a morning to spare. The hard part is remembering they belong to whoever comes after us.
Odo|A river king sounds a little unlikely.|That was the opinion of everyone watching, too. A fisherman deserves at least ten minutes before the truth catches up.
Tolan|You could still put down the spear.|And take what home instead? I ask myself that more often than you might think. Keep your voice down around Bram.
Serjeant Bram|Knowing a name does not make an order fair.|No. But it means I cannot pretend a missing man was merely a number. Do not mistake that for permission to disobey me.
Doran|Does armor make you brave?|It makes the other fellow hesitate. Courage is easier to discuss once he has done that.
Elder Maddock|Two maps sounds like one too many.|Only if they agree. Mine did not. I spent a wet afternoon discovering that neither knew where I was.
Pip|I will try to tread more quietly.|You need not disappear. Just remember that the ground carries your footsteps farther than your voice.
Mycella|What if someone cuts through those roots?|Then a memory loses its road. We grow another, when we can. That does not make the first one unimportant.
Bolete|Could I pull some roots up for you?|Loosen, not tear. We are asking for room, not declaring war on the trees.
Truffle|They seem too small to survive here.|That is why I stay. Being small is a reason to need help, not a reason to go without it.
The Shroom King|A crown sounds like a lot of waiting.|Waiting and listening are different work. The first wears you out. The second sometimes saves everybody a second argument.
Calder|Did anybody ever repair the axle?|Eventually. By then I had a place people were looking for. It is strange how a broken wheel can put you on the right road.
Prue|Would you put your own name on a wall?|Perhaps somewhere small. I would like people to know my work, without having to live inside my signature.
Toft|I would hate being the one who needed help.|Then you would have had a hard first week. Nobody learns a mine by being too proud to let someone check their lamp.
Linna|I prefer the market when it is quiet.|Then come after the shouting. There is a different sort of pleasure in seeing everyone count a good morning's takings.
Wren|I think I would still want a label.|So would I. Learning the smell was a safeguard, not an excuse to keep a badly marked shelf.
Bevan|Could the bruised ones still be used?|For a pie, if you cut away the bad part soon enough. A bruise need not waste an apple, but hiding one can waste a basket.
Isolde|Perhaps your grandmother liked it sweet.|Perhaps. She had a kind way of letting me find that out for myself, and a very large teacup.
Nazim|Will you teach someone to keep it sound?|I had better. A cistern that depends on one pair of hands is already beginning to fail.
Halima|I would rather ask where someone has been.|Good. A smell gives you a question. It does not give you the right to decide the answer.
Tarek|It still sounds like a dangerous animal.|It is. Knowing why I love it does not mean you should stand near its teeth.
Suhaila|Blue birds would look lovely in our house.|Tell her that if you meet her. She says she weaves for herself, but she listens very carefully when someone says where a blanket will go.
Idris|What if one of them never comes home?|I will keep sending letters. A closed door does not shorten a long road.
Rashida|Was it honest to sell an accident?|The bowl was sound, and I showed every mark. The dishonest part was looking as though I had known what I was doing.
Bilal|Perhaps the goat was testing your patience.|It was a thorough examination. I have not named anything Confidence since.
Sella|I am not sure I could eat an ugly fish.|You have eaten stew without asking to meet its ingredients. Let the cook worry about the face.
Ovid|It must be difficult to find any quiet.|There is a pause when one shift ends and the next has not started. I have learned to enjoy it before someone drops a bucket.
Jamila|Could you carry less and make more trips?|On a safe road, certainly. On an uncertain one, every journey costs more than the weight on your back.
Nerissa|I think I would have kept the float too.|Then we would have looked very experienced together. The important part was getting into the water again.
Astrid|Perhaps you could put pretty gloves over warm ones.|Now that is a proposal Runa might tolerate. She has never objected to beauty once the fingers are safe.
Colm|I am usually in a hurry when I eat.|Try remembering what your next meal tastes like. If you cannot, the road has taken something it did not need.
Tessa|I would have wanted to play it perfectly.|So did I. Then somebody enjoyed what I had actually played. That is a useful interruption to perfection.
Rowan the Hunter|Maybe Bramble was training you.|He certainly learned that I replenish the sausages. I am still deciding which of us got the better education.
Sverre|I would be frightened to go out again.|I was. Fear improved my preparations more than pride ever had. I check the shelter before I admire the view now.
Runa|Jam in soup might have been good.|You are welcome to test that in your own pot. Astrid insisted the rest of us deserved supper first.
Eira|Could you write down how much you use?|I do now. Unfortunately the first entry says less than last time. Wisdom arrives in instalments.
Fenton|Your coat must have meant something to you.|It did. Getting home meant more. I still think of it whenever somebody complains about an unfashionable pair of boots.
Tallis|I would find the interruption maddening.|I did. That was rather the point of the lesson. A tune cannot ask the whole world to hold still for it.
Kip|A button can still be treasure.|Exactly. I needed somebody to explain that to the laundress. She thought finding six more had settled the matter.
Ada|Bramble owes you a loaf too.|He has been paying in muddy affection ever since. The interest is extraordinary.
Bren|Was Elowen angry with you?|Disappointed, which lasted longer. She asked me to correct the story with the same care I had used to copy it.
Berta|I ask too many questions as well.|Too many for whom? A tired teacher can put a kettle on. A question swallowed out of politeness may stay unanswered for years.
Della|It is hard to admit you were wrong.|Harder for him than watching her save his child, apparently. Gratitude ought to leave a person a little braver.
Ewan|Perhaps the reader was only having a bad day.|Quite possible. One face is not the whole history. It is still evidence that somebody had to live through the decree.
Fara|I would have been afraid to admit I broke it.|I was. Carrying the pieces home was worse than the breaking. Mother noticed that before she noticed the ornament.
Garrick|You should tell the apprentice that.|I might. A compliment from a stranger would probably do more good than another morning of silent judgement.
Hester|I would have been furious with her.|I was, until the first tear at sea. Then I knew what to do with my hands, even while the rest of me was frightened.
Junia|I hope the lamp is worth all that mending.|Even before I buy it, I have warm feet and fewer broken things. It is an unusually useful way to wait.
Kellan|Perhaps the clock liked the rain.|Then it had an excellent life. I wish it had found a way to enjoy itself without making us miss supper.
Lysa|I would have chosen the perfect bird.|Then there would have been someone for each of them. That seems a good arrangement to me.
Cinder|Would you trust me to carry an ember?|With a sound pot, dry ash, and no running. Being trusted with a flame means deciding that arriving matters more than arriving first.
Warden|You could ask him to knock instead.|I could. But the wheel tells me he is coming while there is still time to put the kettle on.
Ember|Did you apologise to the baker?|Yes. In front of the same people who heard me complain. An apology whispered afterward would have been rather convenient for me.
Dagna|I am glad you let yourself rest.|It took longer to learn than scrubbing. Dust returns whether you have enjoyed your supper or not.
Lode|What happens when a hammer suddenly stops?|I listen for a voice. Familiar noise is comforting because you notice when it changes.
Pike|Why not simply tell him you know?|Because he would make a speech about not needing extra bread. This way two people eat and I am spared the speech.
Hallow|Maybe the mountain needs a better hinge.|I have considered charging it for one. So far it has declined every invitation to discuss the matter.
Quarrel|Does arguing make the bread cheaper?|No, but it makes the waiting pleasant. I would miss the argument if he ever agreed with me.
Flint|Will you pass the lesson on?|Whenever somebody asks. A useful trick grows more valuable when it saves somebody else's wood as well.
Winnie|I would like to see Nan dance again.|Then find a good tune and leave her room. Do not announce that you are doing her a kindness. She will know whose feet are getting tired first.
Ned|Can you show me what to look for?|A pale stretch, a thinning edge, a stitch pulling loose. Looking closely while nothing is broken is the whole trick.
Nan Ferrow|Do you ever sing her songs now?|Sometimes, when my hands are busy and the house is quiet. You need not tiptoe away if you hear me, love. They belonged to you as well.
Joss|You could ask for the cups back.|I could. But I like imagining her using them. Some things are easier to leave behind when you know they are wanted.
Osric|The fellow with the sword might need a safe way home too.|Exactly. I kept telling my brother they ought to travel together. He said that would make the story shorter.
Alder|I would still be nervous around the bees.|Good. Calm is useful; carelessness is not. Give them room and remember whose house you are opening.
Gwyneth|A very long scarf could keep two people warm.|That is kinder than Alder's suggestion of using it to tow a cart. I shall remember that at the next fitting.
Bors|Perhaps he was trying to spare you the worry.|He was trying to spare himself an explanation. I know the difference between a worried silence and a guilty change of chair.
Kiln|I would hide my mistakes in a cupboard.|Then you would have to make room for them forever. On the shelf they can at least do some teaching.
Petra|Why did nobody else check the date?|An alarming story moves faster than a sensible question. I try to keep a question ready.
Raff|A shadow seems a kinder clock.|It does not argue. Though it is very poor at telling you when supper should have been ready on a cloudy day.
Suri|I would have left the lentils behind.|I considered it. Then I remembered they were supper. Hunger is an excellent supervisor of dull work.
Tavin|Did anyone laugh when they noticed?|Everybody claimed to have noticed first. The pack had gone, but apparently our pride was still in the doorway.
Una|What will you send her next?|Something small enough to leave room for a letter. The parcels are an excuse to keep telling each other ordinary things.
Vela|I like the idea of leaving room for mistakes.|So do I. It makes learning less like waiting to be caught doing something wrong.
Wystan|I would have refused to pay for the extra sacks.|A sensible course. I was too embarrassed to admit I had lost count. Embarrassment proved more expensive than the dates.
Rania|I would like to join you one evening.|Bring a chair and something that happened to you. It need not be important. We are very good at discussing small matters.
Latif|Bruised peaches sound like fair payment.|They did to me. Mother checked my sums before handing them over, so I could not improve my wages by inventing change.
Yara|Does fighting the sea get tiring?|Yes. Then the light catches the water and I remember why we put a house here. I oil another hinge.
Doryn|I would trust a person before a gull.|Ask a fisher, then. A sensible one will tell you which birds they were watching.
Bry|I would have laughed, then helped.|That would have been an improvement on most of the audience. I can forgive a laugh from someone holding a cloth.
Coral|Waiting sounds harder than sailing.|I have only done my share of one. I try not to make a competition of the things that frighten us.
Edda|A dry crate does sound like a good table.|At last, somebody who understands my furniture. It has never once wobbled when the rain began.
Fennel|Leaves are nothing to be frightened of.|I know that in daylight. At night a small sensible precaution can do more good than a large sensible argument.
Bjorn|You noticed even when he tried to hide it.|Children notice more than grown people hope. I wish I had known how to offer him the bowl without hurting his pride.
Cap|I sometimes think helping means doing more.|Sometimes it means watching long enough to learn what is needed. That was the part I had skipped.
Ilsa|It must have been hard to leave any growing.|Very. A future meal is difficult to explain to an empty stomach. We learned to protect a little before things grew desperate.
Meriel|That sounds like somebody I would trust.|It is a good beginning. She has had plenty of ordinary days since then to prove it was not merely a gracious moment.
Elin|Perhaps you should finish the sensible errand first.|I did buy the cup. Unfortunately it is now standing beneath a window that looks rather empty.
Maelis|An ungrateful goose sounds about right.|Gratitude was never part of the treatment. A healed wing was quite sufficient payment from a goose.
Archivist Elowen|Were you frightened of what he might do?|Certainly. Courage would be easier if officials arrived looking foolish instead of carrying seals. We copied the names anyway.
Mira|Could the letter be mistaken too?|Yes. Grief and exhaustion can blur a detail. That is why I compare accounts instead of declaring one beyond question.
Oren|I sometimes talk to people who are gone.|You need not turn that into a problem to be solved. Some words are worth saying even when you cannot expect an answer.
Tamsin|Would you let somebody else sit there?|If they needed it. I might mention the repair rather more than necessary, but I would move my books.
Master Iven|I would have been embarrassed.|I was. The pupils learned that a teacher can survive being corrected. That was worth more than saving my dignity.
Brin|Would it be better to leave the door out?|Then someone might mistake an unfinished drawing for a solid wall. I prefer a question people can see.
Nell|Writing the names could put you in danger.|That is why I ask before recording a living person's story. They should not pay for my bravery without choosing to.
Sable|A copied mistake could just be carelessness.|It could. The changes around it are what concern me. A good accusation needs more than one convenient clue.
Pella|I hope you still get to see the coast.|So do I. I want to hear the water rather than point to a painted patch of it. I will take him if I can.
Bess|What if more people came than you had chairs?|Then we stood, and passed plates along. A welcome does not have to wait until all the furniture agrees.
Ronan|Useful vinegar is still worth making.|You sound exactly like Bess. Neither of you appreciates how carefully I was trying to preserve my dignity.
Venn|You should keep trying to deliver it.|I intend to. An address can be wrong without the words inside becoming worthless.
Hobb|I suspect the doorway got the worst of it.|There was a mark. We agreed not to call it damage until everyone had caught their breath.
Edric|Courtesy will not mend a torn coat.|No, but it may persuade someone to show you how. That is why I keep the needle as well.
Dorr|You must miss a proper quiet morning.|Sometimes. Other mornings I like knowing there are people at work without being the person who has to lift the wagon first.
Ser Anwen|Was it worth losing their favour?|Ask the people they wanted left outside the oath. My invitation to a meeting was not the largest thing at stake.
Grusk|I would not trust Dain with the deck again.|Trust him to try something. Once you have established that, the game becomes surprisingly honest.
Fen|I would be afraid of stepping on someone's feet.|Choose someone who can laugh and begin slowly. Apologising is part of the first lesson. Everybody takes it.
Senn|You should have told them why you were happy.|After the game, I did. They objected to my brother giving me what they called an unfair advantage.
Dain|You could just ask where somebody travelled from.|Then they might tell me before I had the pleasure of guessing wrong. You are proposing a very efficient end to my amusement.
Rusk|I would have apologised for wishing him quiet.|I did. He said the fog had improved my taste in conversation. Then he talked through supper as well.
Linnet|A tune should not be something to fear.|No. But people who cannot bear a memory sometimes punish the person keeping it. Humming was her way of holding on.
Puck|That sounds like a rather sharp welcome.|Bess can be sharp without being unkind. The lesson cost her time and saved everybody else's ears.
Vale|Your sister sounds difficult to argue with.|Only when she is right, which she insists is most of the time. The hat has made disproving her inconvenient.
Cerys|I would like to hear those breakfasts.|Bring bread. My sister takes notes and I object to the notes, so we sometimes forget to butter anything.
Nyra|I would rather people simply told the truth.|So would I. Until they do, it helps to notice which hand is hiding the coin.
Maren|A towel seems like such a small thing.|Until you are cold enough that somebody noticing feels enormous. An inn begins with paying attention.
Dunstan|I would want to take the sword down myself.|So did I. My master said I could, as soon as I could explain why the next one would be safer.
Sela|Some mistakes must be beyond saving.|Certainly. Then I keep the lesson and begin again. Pretending every broken thing is an ornament would make me a very poor glazier.
Tam|You should keep a place for the aprons.|I have. A working press is no excuse for leaving everything else in a heap, whatever Joss says.
Celia|I like the ordinary parts of stories best.|They remind us that people had mornings before they became names in an account. Clean shirts deserve a place beside grand speeches.
Ivo|Do you ever use the tools?|When I have a job that suits them. Remembering what he could make is better when it helps me make something of my own.
Merrin|You could send word asking him to visit.|I do. The watching is not a substitute for asking. It is what I do with the part of the waiting I cannot shorten.
Zella|The dramatic holes still need mending.|Of course. Mother never meant to ignore them. She meant that a quiet problem does not become less real beside a noisy one.
Iris|I would have hated burning the stool.|I did. It was still easier than shivering beside a perfectly intact seat. I stack the wood before I admire the furniture now.
Alderic|Keeping the steps clear matters too.|On a dull day I have to remind myself of that. A path someone can use is a better welcome than an impressive account of waiting.
King Halvard|Other people should have a say.|They have a say, boy. Then I decide how much of it deserves to trouble the kingdom. You would do well to learn the distinction.
Cartwright Oswin|At least it lasted through the weddings.|A generous judgement. I shall try repeating it while I am underneath the cart. It may improve my temper.
Miner Marn|I would rather be slow than hurt somebody.|Good. Remember that when the person shouting is wearing better clothes than you. The stones do not recognise rank.
Miner Nerik|You could thank Marn instead of hoping he forgets.|I have. He enjoyed that almost as much as being right. I am beginning to think he earned both.
Snowbuilder Nessa|Did making it help you miss him less?|It gave the missing a shape I could put a scarf around. That was enough on some days.
Orin|I am usually looking for somewhere quiet.|Quiet can be welcoming too. A place to stop should let you decide when you are ready for company.
Weft|I usually lose patience before the thread goes through.|Put it down for a breath. The needle's eye does not grow smaller while you rest, though it certainly feels that way when you hurry.
Dorrick|Could the last thing wait until morning?|Almost always. It is surprisingly bad at admitting that until after I have eaten.
Hask|I do not need anything. I just wanted to talk.|Then you have brought exactly what I was hoping for. There are worse ways to spend a little time.
Garrow|I usually leave the tools where I finished.|Then the next job begins with a search. I prefer to leave my future self something kinder than a missing hammer.
Marek|I find it difficult to sit still.|Give yourself until the cup is empty. A small rest does not need to become a whole afternoon to be worthwhile.
Bregga|What if the bad weather never comes?|Then I have things within reach on a pleasant morning. There are worse mistakes to make.
Torvald|Knowing the way matters more than a bright flame.|Both matter. A good light cannot choose a safe path, and a good path is difficult to follow in the dark.
Ingrid|Could checking become another thing to worry about?|It could, if I kept returning. Once is enough. The point is to let myself settle, not spend the night arguing with the latch.
Sigrun|I would probably forget to replace the cloth.|That is why it has a place of its own. An empty space is a better reminder than discovering you needed it after the rain begins.
Asta|I would put up with a bad seat for a fine view.|For a little while, so would I. But if we are going to talk until evening, I will choose something that forgives my back.
